prompt: Where should I get a sleep study done?
answer:
A sleep study, also known as polysomnography, is a sophisticated test that measures your overall sleep quality while you sleep. It is useful in diagnosing sleep disorders such as sleep apnea, narcolepsy and insomnia. There are different types of sleep studies, including in-home studies and in-laboratory studies. Whether you should have an in-home sleep study or an in-laboratory sleep study depends on the severity of your presumed sleep disorder and the equipment required for the test.

In general, in-home sleep studies involve less equipment and provide data that helps the sleep specialist diagnose more common sleep disorders such as sleep apnea. More severe sleep disorders or symptoms unusual for the presumed sleep disorder, as well as equipment that requires a technician to operate, often require an in-laboratory sleep study. In-laboratory sleep studies are generally conducted at a sleep center and can last one full night (all-night study) or up to 2 days (split-night study). During these studies, patients sleep in a controlled environment while their brain activity, breathing, heart activity, eye movements, limb movements, oxygen levels and sleep phases are monitored.

In the United States, the largest sleep centers are located in New York (New York-Presbyterian Hospital), Chicago (NorthShore University HealthSystem), Boston (Massachusetts General Hospital) and Los Angeles (Cedars-Sinai Medical Center). If diagnosed with a severe sleep disorder, it is also likely the sleep specialist will recommend adjustments to your sleep habits, prescribe certain medications or recommend a sleep surgery to alleviate your symptoms.

While sleep studies can be uncomfortable, they are vital to the diagnosis of your sleep disorder and can only be conducted by a medical professional. If you think you may have a sleep disorder, consult a sleep specialist to determine if you need a sleep study and where to get it done.
